 Knicks Notes: Alvarado, Kolek, Hart, Shamet, Jenkins, Towns
 By Arthur Hill |
 at November 11, 2026 9:03 am 
 Brooklyn native  Jose Alvarado became a fan favorite after being traded to the Knicks in February, but he has dropped out of coach Mike Brown ’s rotation lately, with third-year guard Tyler Kolek taking his place, Kristian Winfield of The New York Daily News writes in a subscriber-only piece. Alvarado’s playing time has fallen to 10.4 minutes per night in five games this season, and he was only used for the final six minutes of Tuesday’s blowout win over Milwaukee. Kolek played 15 minutes, posting 12 points and four assists.
 “We’ll go with who we go with until we feel that it’s time to go to the next guy,” Brown said after the game. “So again, it’s not anything negative right now on Jose or even Tyler when he’s out. They just got to be ready to play when their number’s called, and both of them are trying to do that. … Right now, Tyler’s played pretty good basketball. You know, we’ve strung some games, and, you know, again, those guys are close.” 
 Alvarado received a new three-year, $14.4MM contract over the summer, but Kolek’s recent play has made him a better rotation option. He has 40 assists with just five turnovers this season, giving him the best ratio in the NBA. Alvarado has only gotten on the court at the end of lopsided games in his last three appearances, and he didn’t play at all Saturday in Cleveland. Brown acknowledges that Kolek became the primary backup point guard after Alvarado suffered an ankle injury in the second game of the season.
 “The reality is Jose got hurt. Tyler gave us some good minutes, but at the end of the day, I sat them both down and I told them: ‘Jose, you’re our backup because you ended the season as the backup, but both you guys helped us win last year. Jose in the Finals. Tyler in the Cup Finals,” Brown recalled. “So I feel like both you guys can play and contribute at a high level. So both you guys got to be ready because a change can happen at any time.’” 
 There’s more from New York:
 An illness prevented Josh Hart from returning Tuesday after missing the previous two games with ankle soreness, per Stefan Bondy of The New York Post . Landry Shamet made his third straight start, and Brown is comfortable having him in that role. “With the way our team is built we don’t need anybody to do anything extraordinary. Just go, like Landry said, be yourself, play hard,” Brown said. “… Landry is phenomenal to have as a starter because he’s a two-way player. He has to be guarded and he plays with pace, a lot of other things that we believe in.” 
 New Bucks coach Taylor Jenkins talked to reporters about interviewing for the Knicks’ opening last year before Brown was hired, Bondy adds in a separate story . He and Brown were the viewed as the final contenders for the position. “Very blessed to be where I am right now,” Jenkins said. “But excited to go through the process of interviewing with the Knicks. … Learned a lot about this organization, the high standards they had. And obviously the great work that they had done even leading up to last season. So it was a fun process to be a part of. Hopefully I performed well and it just wasn’t meant to be.” 
 After Karl-Anthony Towns posted his 10th straight double-double on Tuesday, James L. Edwards III of The Athletic calls on Knicks owner James Dolan to pay the All-Star center his market value, even if it puts the team into the second apron.
